articles.title: Meet Uma Kashvi: Delhi Capitals Sign 15-Year-Old All-Rounder In WPL Auction
articles.description: Delhi Capitals have secured a promising young talent for the Women’s Premier League, snapping up 15-year-old Uma Kashvi for Rs 10 lakh at the auction. The Karnataka cricketer has attracted attention for her spin-bowling skills and all-round abilities, earning an opportunity to take the next step in her cricketing journey. Kashvi’s signing puts her among the youngest players to secure a WPL contract, making her one to watch as she prepares for a potential transition to the senior professional stage. Uma Kashvi: Young Talent From Karnataka A right-arm spin-bowling all-rounder, Kashvi has already gained experience beyond the domestic junior circuit. She represented India Under-19 in a series against Sri Lanka Under-19, giving her exposure to international-level competition at an early age. Her ability to contribute with the ball, alongside her potential as an all-rounder, helped bring her into the spotlight ahead of the WPL auction. At just 15, she entered the bidding process as the youngest player on the list and ultimately secured a deal with the Delhi-based franchise. The opportunity could provide valuable exposure to the demands of elite women’s cricket, while placing her alongside established international players and experienced members of the team setup. Jemimah Rodrigues Connection Adds Another Layer Kashvi has previously spoken about receiving mentorship from Jemimah Rodrigues, who is set to lead Delhi Capitals as captain. The connection could offer the youngster an opportunity to learn from one of India’s prominent batters within the franchise environment. For Delhi Capitals, signing Kashvi is a move that brings youth and potential into their squad. While her age means she still has plenty of development ahead, her junior international experience gives her a foundation to build on. The Rs 10 lakh deal marks a significant milestone in Kashvi’s young career. With the WPL offering a platform for emerging Indian cricketers to gain experience alongside established stars, the 15-year-old will be hoping to make the most of her opportunity with Delhi Capitals.

articles.title: IND vs NZ: Four Players Who Could Be Dropped From Playing XI After 3rd T20I Win
articles.description: Team India have taken an unassailable 3-0 lead in the T20I series against New Zealand after registering a convincing win in the third match in Wellington. With the series already in the bag, the Indian team management could use the remaining two games to test its bench strength and give opportunities to players who have not featured regularly. As a result, as many as four changes could be made to India's playing XI for the fourth T20I. Four potential changes to India's playing XI Ishan Kishan could return to the playing XI after recovering from the injury that kept him out of the second and third T20Is. If he is declared fit, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi could make way for the experienced wicketkeeper-batter. Sooryavanshi scored 45 runs in the third match, but India may consider bringing Kishan back without disturbing the opening combination of Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson. Nitish Kumar Reddy has delivered impressive performances in the series, but the team management could decide to rest him for a game as a precautionary measure, given his injury concerns. If that happens, Shivam Dube could come into the side and provide another all-round option. India could also hand Varun Chakaravarthy an opportunity. The spinner is an important part of the team's bowling attack but has been unavailable due to injury. With the series decided, the fourth T20I could offer him a chance to return to action, provided he is fully fit. Another possible change could see Mayank Yadav replace Arshdeep Singh. India have been using three fast bowlers - Prince Yadav, Arshdeep and Bhuvneshwar Kumar. The management may choose to rest Arshdeep for one match and give Mayank an opportunity to showcase his pace and bowling skills. India's probable playing XI for fourth T20I Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson (wicketkeeper), Ishan Kishan, Shreyas Iyer (captain), Tilak Varma, Shivam Dube, Naman Dhir, Varun Chakaravarthy, Mayank Yadav, Prince Yadav and Bhuvneshwar Kumar.
